page: Google Cloud Platform h4d-megamem-192-lssd is an x86_64 architecture instance providing 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 3024.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields approximately 15.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it in an ultra-high memory footprint category. The instance does not feature GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Local persistent storage is heavily provisioned, incorporating 32 local NVMe SSDs totaling 12885 GB. The large directly attached NVMe storage array offers localized data handling capabilities alongside high memory capacity. The vast allocation of 192 dedicated compute threads balances extreme memory density with high-density multicore processing. Because the system features dedicated vCPU allocation and extensive local solid-state capacity, it represents a substantial hardware footprint that minimizes resource sharing at the cost of requiring high utilization to justify infrastructure expenses.

Given the 3024.0 GB memory capacity paired with 12885 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, Google Cloud Platform h4d-megamem-192-lssd is tailored for memory-intensive and storage-heavy enterprise environments. Appropriate workloads include massive in-memory databases, large-scale distributed analytics, high-throughput caching systems, and heavy transactional databases that benefit from collocated high-speed local disk storage and large memory buffers.
description: Google Cloud Platform h4d-megamem-192-lssd is an x86_64 server instance engineered for extreme memory and storage demands. The configuration delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs, 3024.0 GB of system memory, and 12885 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage across 32 local drives, offering 15.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. No GPU acceleration is present, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its massive memory density and high-capacity direct-attached NVMe storage, the instance emphasizes collocated data processing and minimal external storage latency. The dedicated compute allocation ensures consistent performance across high-thread environments, making it suitable for hardware-dense deployments where standard memory capacities are insufficient. This instance is primarily suited for large-scale in-memory databases, complex online transaction processing, intensive enterprise data caching, and large batch analytics workloads that require large active data sets in RAM and high-speed local disk persistence.
